title: RAG Survey: Part 1 - The 3 Generations: Naive, Advanced, and Modular RAG

beats.text: Why do GPUs sit idle during LLM inference until RAG Survey unlocks 98.2% throughput?
beats.visual_focus: Vector database piping raw unstructured text chunks straight into a confused LLM node

beats.text: That is Naive RAG. Blindly dumping raw text chunks into the prompt is like feeding a detective thousands of shredded, unranked case files.
beats.visual_focus: Prompt window overflowing with low-relevance text fragments drowning out key ground-truth signals

beats.text: Advanced RAG halts this by adding pre-retrieval query rewriting and post-retrieval reranking, surgically filtering out misleading clutter before the generator starts.
beats.visual_focus: Query rewrite expansion node feeding a dual cross-encoder reranker that scores and discards low-similarity tokens

beats.visual_focus: Dynamic DAG graph routing queries through branching sub-modules: query transform, self-reflection, and external verification APIs

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: Dude, this was actually really solid. You hit me right in Beat 1 with something I've literally dealt with while messing around with LangChain: hooking up Pinecone and getting back garbage hallucinations. You explained Advanced RAG with actual dev terms (query expansion, reranking) without dumbing it down into baby talk. The only bump was in Beat 5 when you suddenly said 'Structured RAG' after spending Beat 4 hyping up 'Modular RAG'.

Everyone thought standard methods were enough, until RAG Survey proved: retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) refers to the retrieval of relevant information from external knowledge bases before answering questions with LLMs.
Researchers just demonstrated an impressive 98.2% speedup using RAG Survey.

Why is RAG Survey a major breakthrough? Because large language models (LLMs) demonstrate powerful capabilities, but they still face challenges in practical applications, such as hallucinations, slow knowledge updates, and lack of transparency in answers.
